pages.title: The crystal's own
text: The terraced mesas keep a long-necked grazer and a dragonfly in the open, a pill-bug in the caves beneath, and a crystal mantis that walks the crystal at night.

Every gentle beast here can be brushed for its reagent once a minute, and is tempted and bred with its own food, named under **Hunting and herding** below. It can be bonded like any gentle animal (see [familiars](familiars)), and though none has a gift of its own, a bonded one can still take a voice at a totem and strengthen your magic (see [attuning at a totem](familiar_attuning)).

pages.title: Chime Grazer
text: A violet, woolly, long-necked grazer with two great crystal horns and a ridge of crystal along its back, in herds of two to four. **24 health** and **3 armour**.
It drops **1 to 3 Chime Crests**, more with Looting.
Hunted, it also drops 1 to 2 Raw Game, up to 1 March Leather and up to 1 Amethyst Shard. Breed with **wheat**.

pages.title: Glass Flitter
text: A dragonfly with glass wings, in ones to threes. **10 health**, no armour.
Hunted, it also drops up to 2 Feathers. Breed with **Echo Blooms or any small flower**.

pages.title: Geode Grub
text: A heavy pill-bug of banded lilac stone with a pale head plate, a ridge of geodes down its spine, of the dark caves under the mesas, one to three at a time. **26 health** and **5 armour**, very slow, and gentle.
Hunted, it also drops up to 2 Amethyst Shards. Breed with **Lantern Caps or any mushroom**.

pages.title: Shard Stalker
text: A crystal mantis that rises among the crystal at night, one or two at a time. It has **21 health** and **1 armour**, is quick, and its strike does **5** and poisons you for 3 seconds.
It drops **1 to 2 Shard Barbs**, a Venom reagent.
Hunted, it also drops up to 1 Amethyst Shard and up to 1 String.

pages.title: Hunting and herding
text: Besides its reagent, each one drops more when hunted, and more again with Looting. Meat drops roasted if the animal died burning. To breed wild ones, **sneak** while you feed two adults their food; fed normally, a wild one warms to you instead.
